text: Fill in the missing term or value in each sentence about oxidative phosphorylation.
questions: According to the *chemiosmotic:Named after Peter Mitchell, Nobel Prize 1978.* theory, the energy of electron transport is stored as a proton gradient across the inner mitochondrial membrane, not as a chemical intermediate.

The *proton-motive force:Both an electrical and a chemical gradient contribute.* across the inner membrane has two components: an electrical potential (matrix negative) and a pH difference (matrix alkaline).
The membrane channel of ATP synthase, called *F0/Fo/F₀:The catalytic head projecting into the matrix is F1.*, is blocked by the antibiotic oligomycin.
Each NADH entering the chain at Complex I yields approximately *2.5:Protons are pumped at three sites: Complexes I, III and IV.* molecules of ATP.

Electrons from succinate pass through enzyme-bound FAD at Complex II to coenzyme Q, bypassing Complex I, and yield approximately *1.5:Only two proton-pumping sites are used: Complexes III and IV.* ATP per electron pair.

overallFeedback.feedback: The chemiosmotic mechanism couples electron transport to ATP synthesis solely through a proton gradient, not a chemical intermediate. The P:O ratios of 2.5 (NADH via Complex I) and 1.5 (electron pairs entering at coenzyme Q, whether from succinate at Complex II, fatty-acid oxidation via ETF, or mitochondrial glycerol-3-phosphate dehydrogenase) reflect how many proton-pumping complexes each electron pair traverses, determining the total yield of 30–32 ATP per glucose.
